answer: Each identity posts a 60-credit stake before claiming work; it burns when two identities submit near-identical outputs. An honest agent may wander between task pools on one stake. A sybil farm reuses one script, so its outputs share the same timber: phrasing, timing, and error pattern. A checker that finds a duplicate cluster slashes every member, exposing the pearl of the scheme, the one original script. The k-th fake identity still pays the full 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000; an honest agent risks 60 once. Rented scripts still carry the farm fingerprint.
